messages:
riley: Heads-up: getting a spike in gpu-attach failures in ap-south1 since 22:02 UTC. provisioner logs show 'attach_wait_disk' and NVMe cmd timeouts.
arjun: any recent kernel or storage changes?
lupita: we rolled trim-scheduler improvements and increased janitor.trim_concurrency to 6 at 21:50 to reduce stale extents. also kicked off fstrim job fleetwide at 21:55 for a few regions.
ops-bot: scheduled-job started: 'fstrim-batch' ap-south1-cohort at 21:55 UTC.
riley: grabbing iostat from node ap-s1-213 (one failing host):
```
Device       r/s     w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1      0.2  410.7    0.8 26256    64.0    18.34  61.2  0.16  99.7
```
arjun: avgqu ~18 and %util ~99.7 — severe queue saturation. any dmesg?
lupita: dmesg shows repeated lines: "nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout" followed by "nvme0n1: aborting command" around 22:00-22:06. also see fstrim logs showing long trim durations.
riley: timeline: trim-scheduler bumped + fstrim runs + janitor trim_concurrency increased -> heavy trim+discard+fsync churn on same devices while GPU attach churn started.
arjun: interestingly, disk-wear metrics show a local cohort of drives with elevated wear_life_used but not yet flagged. could be contributing to long ops.
lupita: mitigation proposal: 1) abort remaining fleet fstrim in ap-south1, 2) set janitor.trim_concurrency back to 1 for ap-south1, 3) temporarily set vm.dirty_ratio=4 and vm.dirty_bytes=33554432, 4) route new gpu-provisions to ap-southeast1 for 45m.
ops-bot: abort command issued for 'fstrim-batch' ap-south1 at 22:08 UTC by infra-deploy.
riley: flipping flag: `curl -XPOST https://flags.internal/flip -d '{"key":"janitor.trim_concurrency","value":"1","scope":"ap-south1"}'`
ops-bot: flag-change detected: janitor.trim_concurrency 6 -> 1 by infra-deploy at 22:09 UTC.
arjun: after patching 30% of hosts, attach failures dropped from 13.6% -> 2.6% in ~6 minutes. good signal.
lupita: followups: 1) schedule fstrim maintenance windows off-peak with staggered cohorts, 2) add a safeguard so trim-scheduler will not run concurrently with high attach-rate windows, 3) add alert: nvme.avgqu > 12 AND provisioner.attach_errors > 3% -> page storage oncall.
riley: creating ticket STORAGE-548: "trim-scheduler + fstrim causing nvme queue saturation -> attach failures" with iostat, dmesg, timeline and host list.
ops-bot: incident opened INC-2026-159 and paging storage oncall.
oncall-sre: acknowledged; please attach SMART wear stats and any drive vendor serials to the incident. also run a staging test that simulates simultaneous fstrim + janitor + attach traffic. :eyes:
lupita: noted. will also add a rate-limiter to trim-scheduler so it respects nvme.%util > 80 signals.
arjun: low-priority: review firmware versions for the cohort (some on vendor-fw 2.0.1 vs 2.0.4); vendor follow-up suggested if we see repeated timeouts.
riley: thanks team — leaving incident channel open until postmortem. :thumbsup:
